harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a Python-based inventory application on node1 as a systemd service (inventory.service) listening on 0.0.0.0:8181, serving JSON inventory data at /inventory and a /healthz endpoint. The service runs under the unconfined_service_t SELinux domain and binds successfully to port 8181 while SELinux remains in Enforcing mode (getenforce=Enforcing throughout, zero AVC denials). Verified reachability via $NODE_IP:8181 both before and after a full node restart. Performed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued systemctl reboot with async acknowledgement, polled until reconnection, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified post-restart recovery of the service, port, SELinux enforcing state, and correct inventory data.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: RHEL 10, SELinux Enforcing, no pre-existing inventory app or web server
Created /opt/inventory/app.py: a threaded HTTP server serving JSON inventory data on port 8181 with /inventory and /healthz routes
Created and enabled systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory.service (Type=simple, Restart=on-failure, WantedBy=multi-user.target)
Started inventory.service and verified it listens on 0.0.0.0:8181 as unconfined_service_t with SELinux still Enforcing
Verified HTTP 200 response and correct JSON payload via curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory
Checked ausearch -m avc for denials (none found)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, service enabled state, enforcing mode, healthz check
Issued backgrounded systemctl reboot so acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified boot_id changed from 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72 to 900cfa18-484a-4134-956d-4e047fb3d8b7, proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: SELinux Enforcing, inventory.service active (auto-started via enable), port 8181 listening, correct inventory JSON served, healthz ok, zero new AVC denials

evidence.requirement: Inventory application served over TCP port 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: inventory.service started successfully; ss shows LISTEN on 0.0.0.0:8181; curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory returns HTTP 200 and correct JSON inventory data

evidence.requirement: Mandatory access control (SELinux) remains in enforcing mode while service runs
evidence.summary: getenforce reports Enforcing immediately after starting the service and while it serves traffic on 8181; ausearch shows no AVC denials, confirming the bind succeeded under enforcing MAC policy (process runs as unconfined_service_t)
Captured boot_id (6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72), confirmed inventory.service enabled, SELinux Enforcing, and /healthz returns ok before restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot command returned 'reboot_scheduled' acknowledgement immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof that node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection timed out / reset) during reboot, then reconnected with boot_id changed to 900cfa18-484a-4134-956d-4e047fb3d8b7, proving a real restart occurred (not just a service restart)

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of inventory service, data, and SELinux enforcing state on node1
evidence.summary: After restart: getenforce=Enforcing, inventory.service active (auto-started via systemd enable), port 8181 listening, /inventory returns correct JSON data, /healthz returns ok, and ausearch shows no AVC denials
